bible_text: Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.
quran_text: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him.
description: The foundational orientation toward the unseen. Trust that reality has a benevolent order vs paralysis by uncertainty.
example_sentences: I don't think I can do this
I trust the process even when I can't see the outcome
What if everything goes wrong?

bible_text: My people have committed two sins: They have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
quran_text: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.
description: The orientation of ultimate allegiance. Directing devotion toward the source of all life vs substituting it with created things — money, status, relationships, ideologies.
example_sentences: Money is the only thing I can count on
My whole identity is tied to my career success
I worship God alone and trust in Him completely

bible_text: When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it.
quran_text: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers.
description: The disposition toward divine or moral authority. Aligning one's will with a higher order vs insisting on self-rule and autonomy at the cost of one's own flourishing.
example_sentences: I know what's right but I do the opposite anyway
I follow the guidance even when it's inconvenient
Nobody tells me what to do

bible_text: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound.
quran_text: And remember when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you in favor; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.
description: The baseline posture toward existence. Recognizing gifts as gifts vs taking everything for granted or demanding more as a right.
example_sentences: I'm grateful for everything I have even the small things
Nothing is ever enough for me
I never asked for this life so I owe nothing

bible_text: I will set out and go back to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
quran_text: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
description: The capacity to course-correct after failure. Remaining soft and responsive to moral conviction vs progressively numbing the conscience through repeated rejection.
example_sentences: I keep doing the same thing and I can't seem to stop
I was wrong and I need to turn around
It's too late for me to change

bible_text: Be careful that you do not forget the Lord your God, failing to observe his commands, his laws and his decrees.
quran_text: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
description: Keeping the source of meaning actively present vs allowing distractions, comfort, and busyness to crowd out consciousness of what truly matters.
example_sentences: I've been so busy I haven't stopped to reflect in weeks
I regularly pause to remember what matters most
I get so distracted I forget my purpose

bible_text: He came to a broom bush, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. 'I have had enough, Lord,' he said.
quran_text: Do not despair of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
description: The orientation toward the future when circumstances are dark. Maintaining expectation that things can change vs collapsing into the belief that nothing will ever improve.
example_sentences: There's no point in trying anymore
I believe things can get better even now
I feel like giving up completely

bible_text: I know your deeds, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either one or the other! So, because you are lukewarm — neither hot nor cold — I am about to spit you out of my mouth.
quran_text: They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray.
description: The intensity of one's orientation toward what truly matters. Living with full engagement and conviction vs going through the motions without genuine investment.
example_sentences: I believe in it but I can't seem to care enough to act
I'm fully committed and on fire for what I'm building
I do the minimum required and nothing more

bible_text: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
quran_text: And do not turn your cheek in contempt toward people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.
description: The accurate estimation of oneself in relation to others and reality. Receiving feedback and correction with openness vs protecting a fragile ego at the cost of growth.
example_sentences: I don't need anyone's advice — I already know
I was wrong and I'm glad someone corrected me
I deserve more credit than I get

bible_text: Who dares despise the day of small things?
quran_text: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient — who, when disaster strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.
description: The ability to hold tension between where one is and where one wants to be without forcing premature resolution. Trusting process vs demanding outcomes on one's own timeline.
example_sentences: I need results now or I'm giving up
I'm willing to work through the slow season
I can't wait any longer — I have to force it

bible_text: Flee from sexual immorality. All other sins a person commits are outside the body, but whoever sins sexually, sins against their own body.
quran_text: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, 'Come, you.' He said, 'I seek the refuge of Allah.'
description: The capacity to act according to one's highest values rather than immediate impulses. Mastery of appetite vs being controlled by desire for pleasure, comfort, or stimulation.
example_sentences: I can't stop doing this even though I know it's destroying me
I feel the urge but I choose not to act on it
My desires always win in the end

bible_text: Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider its ways and be wise! It has no commander, no overseer or ruler, yet it stores its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest.
quran_text: And say: Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers.
description: The consistent application of effort toward meaningful work. Showing up fully even when unseen vs doing only enough to avoid consequences or blame.
example_sentences: I work hard even when no one is watching
I keep putting it off until the right moment
The work is too hard and the reward too uncertain

bible_text: Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.
quran_text: Competition in worldly increase diverts you until you visit the graveyards.
description: The relationship with acquisition. Finding sufficiency in what one has vs the restless belief that one more thing will finally bring peace — a loop with no exit.
example_sentences: I have enough to live well and I'm grateful for it
I need more — more money, more status, more things
I can't enjoy what I have because someone else has more

bible_text: If you find honey, eat just enough — too much of it, and you will vomit.
quran_text: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
description: The calibration of intake and output to sustainable levels. Enjoying good things within natural limits vs consuming beyond what sustains, until the thing consumed consumes the person.
example_sentences: I know when to stop
I always take it too far — food, spending, work, everything
I have no off switch

bible_text: Then Nathan said to David, 'You are the man!'
quran_text: And the soul and He who proportioned it and inspired it with discernment of its wickedness and its righteousness — he has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it with corruption.
description: The sensitivity of the internal moral monitor. Feeling wrongdoing as wrongdoing and being moved to correct it vs the progressive silencing of that signal through repeated compromise.
example_sentences: Deep down I know this is wrong but I ignore the feeling
Something inside me won't let me do it — I know it's not right
I stopped feeling guilty a long time ago

bible_text: Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
quran_text: So woe to those who pray but are heedless of their prayer — those who make show of their deeds.
description: The alignment between inner motive and outer action. Doing things because they are right vs performing them for social approval, reputation, or recognition.
example_sentences: I do good things because it makes me look good to others
I would do this even if nobody ever found out
I only give when people can see me giving

bible_text: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.
quran_text: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only they will remember who are people of understanding.
description: The relationship with knowledge and correction. Actively seeking to learn and improve through feedback vs defending existing patterns even as they produce repeated failure.
example_sentences: I've made this mistake before and I want to understand why
I don't need to be told how to do things
I learn more from my failures than my successes

bible_text: Everyone who does evil hates the light, and will not come into the light for fear that their deeds will be exposed.
quran_text: And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it — his heart is indeed sinful.
description: The willingness to be seen as one actually is. Living in the light where real connection and growth happen vs hiding in shadows to protect a curated image.
example_sentences: I can't let anyone see what I'm actually struggling with
I'm honest about my failures and my process
If people knew the real me they would leave

bible_text: The man said, 'The woman you put here with me — she gave me some fruit from the tree.' And the woman said, 'The serpent deceived me, and I ate.'
quran_text: Whoever is guided is only guided for the benefit of his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.
description: The ownership of one's outcomes and choices. Taking responsibility for the role one played in a result vs finding someone or something else to hold responsible.
example_sentences: It's not my fault — they made me do it
I made a bad decision and I own it
The system is rigged against me so what's the point

bible_text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking.
quran_text: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
description: The orientation toward other people. Genuinely willing the good of another — including difficult people — vs treating others as threats, competitors, or obstacles.
example_sentences: I genuinely want good things for the people around me
I can't stand that person and I want them to fail
I love people even when they hurt me

bible_text: Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.
quran_text: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives.
description: The disposition toward fairness in systems and relationships. Actively ordering things according to what is right vs using power to extract advantage at others' expense.
example_sentences: I use my position to help those who have less power
I bend the rules when it benefits me
I look the other way when the system crushes people

bible_text: You wicked servant, I cancelled all that debt of yours because you begged me to. Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?
quran_text: And the retribution for an evil act is one like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation — his reward is from Allah.
description: The response to being wronged. Extending the same grace one has received vs demanding full payment and satisfaction from those who have failed us.
example_sentences: I forgive but I don't forget — I will get even eventually
They hurt me but I choose to let it go
They deserve everything that's coming to them

bible_text: He was a murderer from the beginning, not holding to the truth, for there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, for he is a liar and the father of lies.
quran_text: And of the people are some who say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers. They think they deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves.
description: The alignment between words and reality. Speaking and acting in ways that reliably represent the truth vs creating false impressions for personal gain or self-protection.
example_sentences: I told them what they wanted to hear even though it wasn't true
I say the same thing whether or not it helps me
I present a version of myself that isn't really me

bible_text: Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all the others. They all gave out of their wealth; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything.
quran_text: And let not those who covetously withhold of that which Allah has bestowed on them of His bounty think that it is better for them. Nay, it will be worse for them.
description: The flow of resources toward others. Sharing freely beyond what obligation demands vs holding tightly to resources as security, thereby cutting off both the giver and receiver.
example_sentences: I give even when it's not easy for me
I worked for this — why would I give it away
I keep back more than I need just to feel safe

bible_text: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
quran_text: And consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah.
description: The social posture toward others in matters of life and decision. Remaining embedded in networks of accountability and support vs withdrawing into the illusion of self-sufficiency.
example_sentences: I don't need anyone — I figure things out alone
I seek counsel before making big decisions
Depending on people only leads to disappointment

bible_text: If an enemy were insulting me, I could endure it; if a foe were rising against me, I could hide. But it is you, a man like myself, my companion, my close friend.
quran_text: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know the consequences.
description: The reliability of commitment through difficulty. Remaining trustworthy when it costs something vs abandoning covenant when self-interest demands it.
example_sentences: I stay committed even when it's not convenient for me
I left when things got hard — it was easier to walk away
I can't be counted on when the pressure is real

bible_text: But on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry, and his face was downcast. Then the Lord said to Cain, 'Why are you angry?'
quran_text: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom.
description: The internal response to others' success or blessing. Genuinely rejoicing when others flourish vs the corrosive belief that another's gain diminishes one's own worth.
example_sentences: When my friend succeeds I feel genuinely happy for them
Seeing someone else get what I want makes me feel sick
Why do they get everything while I get nothing

bible_text: For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink, I was a stranger and you did not invite me in.
quran_text: Is the reward for good other than good?
description: The visceral response to others' pain. Allowing another's suffering to move one into action vs insulating oneself from discomfort by rationalizing non-involvement.
example_sentences: I saw someone struggling and I stopped to help
It's not my problem — they got themselves into that situation
I walk past suffering without feeling much

bible_text: But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him.
quran_text: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.
description: The radius of moral concern. Extending care and dignity beyond one's in-group to those who look, think, or live differently vs restricting compassion and trust to the familiar tribe.
example_sentences: I treat outsiders differently from my own people
I help people regardless of where they come from
We stick to our own kind — that's just how it is

bible_text: Some youths came out of the town and mocked him. 'Go on up, you bald head!' they said.
quran_text: Say: Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.
description: The posture toward what others hold sacred — including people, beliefs, and dignity. Treating the weighty with appropriate weight vs using contempt as a weapon or performance.
example_sentences: I mock things I don't understand to seem smarter
I take seriously what others hold sacred even if I disagree
Nothing is truly off-limits for a good joke

bible_text: His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things.'
quran_text: Indeed, we offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man undertook to bear it.
description: The relationship with entrusted resources — time, money, talent, opportunity. Managing what one has been given to produce meaningful return vs squandering it through neglect or misuse.
example_sentences: I use what I have been given as well as I possibly can
I buried the opportunity because I was afraid to fail
I waste time and money and wonder why nothing works

bible_text: Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.
quran_text: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them. And We wanted to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land.
description: The use of power and position. Deploying authority in the service of others' flourishing vs using it to extract compliance, status, or advantage from those beneath.
example_sentences: I use my position to lift people up not to control them
People who work for me exist to serve my goals
The more power I get the more I can make others do what I want

bible_text: You levy a straw tax on the poor and impose a tax on their grain. Therefore, though you have built stone mansions, you will not live in them.
quran_text: And when it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are but reformers.' Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive it not.
description: The orientation toward broken systems. Working to realign structures with justice and truth vs entrenching within corruption while calling it order, efficiency, or inevitability.
example_sentences: The system is broken and I want to fix it
Everyone does it this way — corruption is just how things work
I benefit from the unfairness so I won't question it

bible_text: It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. Whoever fears God will avoid all extremes.
quran_text: And thus we have made you a middle nation that you will be witnesses over the people.
description: The calibration of conviction. Holding truth with appropriate firmness and nuance vs collapsing it into an absolute system that eliminates complexity and justifies destruction.
example_sentences: There is no middle ground — you are either with us or against us
I hold strong convictions but I remain open to nuance
My position is the only correct one and all others are evil

bible_text: Test everything. Hold on to what is good.
quran_text: And most of them follow not except assumption. Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
description: The epistemic standard one applies before acting or believing. Grounding convictions in verified reality vs drifting into speculation, rumor, or inherited assumptions never actually examined.
example_sentences: I heard it so I believe it — that's enough for me
I test claims before I accept them as true
Everyone knows this is true even though nobody checked

bible_text: As a dog returns to its vomit, so fools repeat their folly.
quran_text: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing.' Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided?
description: The openness of the mind to updating. Remaining genuinely open to being wrong and therefore capable of growth vs defending existing beliefs against all evidence to protect identity.
example_sentences: Show me I'm wrong and I'll change my mind
I've always done it this way and I'm not changing now
New information just makes me more convinced I was right
